questions.question: Describe the structure of a nucleotide and explain its role in DNA.
questions.solution:
A **nucleotide** consists of: (1) a pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA), (2) a nitrogenous base (A,T,G,C in DNA), (3) a phosphate group.

In DNA, nucleotides form a double helix via complementary base pairing (A-T, G-C) connected by hydrogen bonds.
questions.knowledgeNote: DNA = deoxyribonucleic acid; RNA = ribonucleic acid. DNA stores genetic info; RNA transfers it.
questions.answer: **Structure of a nucleotide:** the monomer of nucleic acids, made of **three parts covalently linked:** (1) a **pentose sugar** — deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA; (2) a **nitrogenous base** attached to the sugar's 1′ carbon — a **purine** (adenine, double ring; or guanine) or a **pyrimidine** (cytosine, thymine in DNA, or uracil in RNA — single ring); (3) a **phosphate group** esterified to the sugar's 5′ carbon — giving the nucleotide its acid character and negative charge. (A sugar + base without phosphate = **nucleoside**; adding the phosphate makes the **nucleotide**.) **Role in DNA:** nucleotides are the **building blocks of the DNA polymer** — the 5′-phosphate of one nucleotide bonds to the 3′-OH of the next, forming the **sugar–phosphate backbone** (a phosphodiester chain); the **sequence of bases along the chain is the genetic code**, and complementary base pairing (A=T with two H-bonds, G≡C with three) lets the two strands hold the double helix together and serve as templates for exact replication. **Deep point:** the nucleotide is a three-part code letter — sugar and phosphate form the chain's spine, the base is the letter; DNA's information content is nothing more than the order of those letters.
